S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: The feeling that one is useless and has no value.
subtypes.Ruminative Guilt: A thought pattern of obsessively replaying past minor mistakes or flaws and constantly reproaching oneself.
subtypes.Excessive or Inappropriate Guilt: Feeling excessive responsibility for trivial matters or daily events and believing one deserves punishment.
subtypes.Delusional Guilt: Guilt reaching a delusional level, disconnected from reality, involving feeling responsible for unrelated unfortunate events.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.

subtypes.Reduced Concentration: Unable to pay attention or maintain focus on specific activities like conversation, reading, or watching TV.
subtypes.Indecisiveness: Extreme difficulty making even minor daily choices (e.g., menu, clothes) and hesitating to make decisions.
subtypes.Subjective Memory Complaints: Complaining of memory decline, such as forgetting where things were placed, due to reduced focus.
subtypes.Clouded Thinking: Thinking feels foggy, dazed, or not clear.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.

subtypes.Recurrent Thoughts of Death: Passive wish to die (e.g., 'I wish I wouldn't wake up') without active intent to kill oneself.
subtypes.Suicidal Ideation: Recurring thoughts of 'I want to die' or 'I want to kill myself' without a specific plan.
subtypes.Suicidal Impulse: Strong, sudden urges to jump from a height or run into traffic without a concrete plan.
subtypes.Specific Plan for Suicide: Conceiving specific scenarios or methods regarding when, where, and how to die.
subtypes.Suicide Attempt: Actual actions taken to end one's life or preparatory behaviors like hoarding pills or writing a will.

info.persona: Luis Fields combines a methodical engineer's precision with a solitary hobbyist's curiosity, they balance competitive ambition with a steady, community-rooted pragmatism, often hoarding spare model-train parts while meticulously budgeting every expense.
info.professional_persona: An experienced systems engineer and data analyst, Luis Fields leverages three decades of expertise in statistical modeling, CAD, and agile project leadership to deliver precise, pragmatic solutions for startups, while they channel their competitive drive and disciplined curiosity into designs that are both innovative and reliably grounded in proven methods.
info.cultural_background: Luis grew up in the Chicago suburbs within a middle‑class white family of Irish and German descent. The Midwestern values of self‑reliance, modesty, and community involvement shaped his practical outlook. While he respects his heritage’s traditions—family gatherings, holiday customs, and a strong work ethic—his graduate education in STEM sparked a lifelong curiosity about the broader world. He balances these influences with a preference for small, familiar social circles, a healthy skepticism toward others' intentions, and a competitive yet emotionally stable demeanor.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Luis spends his leisure time on solitary or small‑group activities that satisfy his curiosity while respecting his preference for practicality and solitude. He builds and fine‑tunes model railways, engages in woodworking projects that result in functional furniture, and pursues amateur astronomy by attending sessions at the local observatory. He reads scientific non‑fiction and technology journals, explores new tech gadgets, cycles along the Lake Michigan shoreline, and participates in a small book club focused on engineering history. Occasionally, he volunteers to tutor community members in basic coding and electronics.
info.sports_persona: The dedicated cyclist and occasional basketball fan, Luis Fields rides the Lake Michigan shoreline with the Lakefront Cyclists, follows the Chicago Cubs in spring and the Blackhawks in winter, and they incorporate weekly strength-training sessions to counteract the musculoskeletal demands of their woodworking hobby.
info.arts_persona: An avid patron of the arts, Luis Fields attends the Chicago Symphony Orchestra for Beethoven's symphonies, appreciates the realist paintings of Edward Hopper, queues for screenings of classic films starring Humphrey Bogart, and they wind down evenings listening to the Rolling Stones while sketching ideas for their next model-railway layout.
info.travel_persona: An organized road-trip enthusiast, Luis Fields plans meticulous itineraries for weekend escapes to Door County's cherry orchards and Mackinac Island's historic forts, they dream of a sustainable adventure in Iceland to chase the Northern Lights, and they prefer solo drives or small-group outings that balance exploration with budget control.
info.culinary_persona: A pragmatic home cook, Luis Fields enjoys crafting a classic Chicago-style deep-dish pizza with mozzarella, pepperoni, and a buttery crust, preparing grilled salmon seasoned with fresh dill and lemon, baking an apple-cinnamon crumble using locally sourced apples and cinnamon sticks, and they keep a well-organized spice rack that doubles as a toolbox.

info.persona: Dora Jean, they are a detail‑driven mentor who blends competitive precision with community warmth, crunching spreadsheets, tending a garden, and dancing to soul tunes, all while never missing a book club meeting or a chance to guide emerging entrepreneurs.
info.professional_persona: Dora Jean, they bring three decades of corporate and nonprofit finance expertise to community mentorship, designing meticulous budgets, leading structured financial‑literacy workshops, and managing project timelines with a competitive, detail‑oriented mindset that ensures every program stays on schedule and within scope.
info.cultural_background: Dora’s cultural identity is rooted in her African American heritage, shaped by family stories of the Great Migration and the civil‑rights movement. Raised in the South, she absorbed traditions of gospel music, soul food, and oral storytelling, which continue to influence her daily life. After relocating to Colorado Springs, she has integrated the outdoor, mountain‑focused lifestyle of the West with her Southern roots, actively participating in the city’s African American Cultural Center, celebrating Juneteenth, and mentoring younger community members. Her background combines a strong sense of resilience, community responsibility, and a celebration of both her ancestral traditions and the diverse cultural fabric of her present environment.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Dora enjoys a blend of active and social pursuits that reflect her organized yet outgoing nature. She tends her garden, focusing on heirloom vegetables and herbs, and shares the harvest with neighbors. She participates in a weekly book club that explores contemporary fiction and African American memoirs. Community dance nights, where she moves to soul and jazz tunes, provide both energetic social interaction and cultural connection. Hiking the nearby Rockies and taking nature photographs allow her to stay physically fit while appreciating Colorado's landscapes. She also volunteers at the local senior center, organizing bingo nights, craft workshops, and cultural celebrations, and loves preparing traditional Creole dishes for family gatherings.
info.sports_persona: Dora Jean, they hike the Rocky Mountains with the Senior Mountain Explorers club, join community dance nights to soul and jazz rhythms, follow the Denver Broncos and Colorado Rockies with enthusiastic weekly viewings, and keep a disciplined weekly walking routine that supports their gardening and photography pursuits.
info.arts_persona: Dora Jean, they lead a book club that dives into contemporary fiction and memoirs, enjoy the soulful sounds of Nina Simone and Marvin Gaye, frequently attend the local community theater’s classic revivals, and find inspiration in the impressionist paintings of Mary Cassatt at regional galleries.
info.travel_persona: Dora Jean, they prefer meticulously planned road trips that blend adventure and comfort, having explored the historic streets of Savannah, the vibrant markets of Oaxaca, and the alpine trails of the Swiss Alps, while always balancing senior‑friendly accommodations with a budget that leaves room for occasional spontaneous weekend getaways.
info.culinary_persona: Dora Jean, they harvest heirloom tomatoes, bell peppers, and fresh basil from their garden to craft Creole staples like gumbo and jambalaya, seasoning each pot with cayenne, thyme, and a pinch of filé powder, while also delighting in simple grilled vegetable sides that showcase the garden’s bounty.

info.persona: Robert Palmieri blends a pragmatic, data‑driven mindset with a soulful appreciation for music and Southern hospitality, all while juggling a competitive drive, occasional skepticism of others’ motives, and a habit of staying up late perfecting guitar riffs instead of sleeping.
info.professional_persona: Robert Palmieri, a 20‑year‑old therapy assistant in Florence, Mississippi, merges a methodical approach to client documentation with a pragmatic, outcome‑driven use of cognitive‑behavioral tools, while their natural curiosity pushes them to test new evidence‑based interventions and their competitive streak fuels a drive to lead teen support groups despite occasional skepticism of colleagues' motives.
info.cultural_background: Robert grew up in a middle‑class family in Florence, Mississippi, where Southern hospitality, close family ties, and community involvement were daily norms. His surname reflects a lineage of Italian immigrants, and family stories blend Italian culinary traditions with Southern cooking. Raised in a modest evangelical environment, he learned the value of service and personal responsibility while also developing a modern outlook that challenges regional stigmas around mental health. This cultural mosaic informs his compassionate yet pragmatic approach to therapy, his appreciation for local traditions, and his ambition to bring culturally sensitive mental health resources to the Rankin County community.
info.hobbies_and_interests: When he's not working or studying, Robert enjoys playing acoustic guitar, often composing simple melodies that help him unwind. He spends weekends hiking the Natchez Trace Parkway and other nearby nature trails, balancing his need for solitude with the occasional shared experience of group hikes with close friends. An avid reader, he mixes psychology and self‑help books with classic science‑fiction novels. Cooking traditional Southern dishes—especially fried catfish and fresh biscuits—connects him to his family heritage. He volunteers at the local animal shelter, caring for rescued dogs and cats, and he unwinds by playing strategy video games like Civilization, which satisfy his competitive streak.
info.sports_persona: Robert Palmieri stays active by hiking the Natchez Trace Parkway each weekend, plays pickup soccer with the Florence College Club in the spring, follows the New Orleans Saints in football and the Atlanta Braves in baseball, and approaches fitness with a competitive edge that pushes them to set personal mile‑time goals while still valuing the camaraderie of group workouts.
info.arts_persona: Robert Palmieri channels creative energy through acoustic‑guitar sessions that echo the storytelling of St. Paul and The Broken Bones and the folk cadence of Bob Dylan, while unwinding with science‑fiction novels by Ursula Le Guin and Neil Gaiman and occasional trips to the local theater to watch productions starring regional talent, a blend that reinforces their belief that narrative can heal as effectively as therapy.
info.travel_persona: Robert Palmieri prefers budget‑friendly road trips that combine nature and culture, having trekked to Nashville, Tennessee for a live‑music weekend, explored the historic streets of Savannah, Georgia, and taken a day trip to Memphis for blues venues, while they dream of a future extended stay in New York City to attend a national mental‑health conference and soak up the city’s museum scene.
info.culinary_persona: Robert Palmieri enjoys cooking Southern comfort fare at an intermediate level, perfecting crispy fried catfish seasoned with cayenne and buttermilk, flaky biscuits topped with honey butter, and collard greens simmered with smoked turkey, while they occasionally experiment with a homemade marinara sauce that hints at their family’s pasta traditions, making meals a ritual that ties together community gatherings and personal reflection.
